leaves.name: Documents page — three-pane layout
acceptance: Three-pane layout: folder tree (left), breadcrumb + document list (centre), no persistent right drawer. Folder tree renders system folders sorted before user-created folders; chevron toggle expands nested children. Selecting a folder loads its non-deleted head documents. Breadcrumb reflects the full path from project root.
leaves.evidence: buildTree groups folders by parent_id and sorts system-first. pathOf walks parent_id chain for breadcrumb. Auto-select on first load picks system_kind='plans' if present. useFolders fetches all document_folders ordered by is_system desc, name asc.
gaps: Folder drag-and-drop is absent; moveFolder mutation exists in useFolders (line 96) but no drag-source or drop-target UI is wired — folder reorganisation requires direct DB access.
Tree auto-expansion opens ancestors of the auto-selected 'plans' folder (line 148-153) but does not persist expanded state in localStorage — every page reload collapses the tree.

buildTree does not sort user-created child folders independently by name; they are sorted by the same comparator as top-level folders, so a user folder inserted between two system folders can appear out-of-order if its name sorts earlier than a sibling system folder name.

leaves.name: Folder tree — recursive render, counts, create/rename/delete
acceptance: Folder tree correctly renders nested hierarchy from parent_id. System folders sort before user folders alphabetically. Folder file counts reflect only non-deleted, non-superseded (head) documents. PM/admin can create, rename, delete (empty) folders; inspectors cannot.
leaves.evidence: buildTree produces a Map<parentId, FolderRow[]> with sorted arrays. folderCountsQuery loads all non-deleted project documents once, computes head set by subtracting replaced IDs, and counts by folder_id. createFolder/renameFolder/deleteFolder mutations call Supabase and invalidate the folders query key.
gaps: folderCountsQuery fetches the entire project documents table (all columns) to compute counts — a SELECT * equivalent. A COUNT(*) group-by query would be significantly lighter for projects with large document sets.

deleteFolder on the client calls supabase.from('document_folders').delete() without a prior empty-check in the hook — the server-side block-nonempty trigger (trg_document_folders_block_nonempty) prevents the delete, but the client receives a PostgreSQL RAISE EXCEPTION error message, which is surfaced as a destructive toast with the raw SQL message rather than a friendlier UI-level guard.

System folders can be renamed via the same useFolders.renameFolder mutation; no guard in the mutation or RLS prevents a PM from renaming 'Plans' to an arbitrary name, breaking the system_kind visual hint in KIND_HINTS.

leaves.name: 10 standard seeded folders auto-created on project insert
acceptance: Every new project automatically receives 10 system folders: Plans, Specs, RFIs, Submittals, Shop Drawings, Change Orders, Daily Reports, Photos, As-Builts, Correspondence. Existing projects are backfilled. seed_project_standard_folders is idempotent (ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING).
leaves.evidence: seed_project_standard_folders inserts 10 rows (is_system=true) with system_kind values mapping each folder name. trg_projects_seed_folders fires AFTER INSERT ON projects. Backfill DO block iterates all existing projects and calls the same function.
gaps: The backfill block also inserts legacy PDF rows into plans/specs folders — if projects.pdf_storage_path or specs_storage_path references a blob that was already deleted from storage, the inserted document row becomes a dangling reference with no storage object.

ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING relies on the partial unique indexes uq_document_folders_top_name and uq_document_folders_child_name. The seed inserts all 10 folders at the top level (parent_id=NULL), so the top-level unique index covers them — correct. However if a user manually created a folder named 'Plans' before the migration ran, the conflict suppresses the system-folder insert and that folder remains non-system with no system_kind, breaking role-gating.
No AFTER INSERT trigger on document_folders validates that exactly 10 system folders exist post-seed; drift from the expected set is not detected at runtime.

leaves.name: File upload with per-file progress queue and same-name versioning
acceptance: Uploading a file with the same name as an existing document in the same folder automatically creates a new version (version + 1) linked via replaces_document_id. Upload queue shows per-file pending/uploading/done/error status. Completed items auto-clear after 5 s; failures persist until dismissed.
leaves.evidence: runUploads in Documents.tsx performs a folder-scoped query for existing documents, builds a latestByName Map filtering replaced IDs, then uploads to project-documents storage and inserts a documents row with replaces_document_id set if a prior version exists. uploadFiles in useDocuments.ts is a parallel implementation with the same logic. Per-file UploadItem state drives the queue UI. setTimeout auto-clears done items at 5000 ms.
gaps: runUploads in Documents.tsx and uploadFiles in useDocuments.ts are duplicate upload implementations with slightly different error paths — the page-level runUploads propagates per-file error status to the queue UI; the hook-level uploadFiles surfaces a single toast on first error and aborts remaining files. Both code paths can be triggered; only runUploads is used for the main upload drag/drop/button flow, but uploadFiles is exported and could be called inconsistently.

The same-name version check queries deleted_at-filtered documents implicitly (it does not filter .is('deleted_at', null)). A soft-deleted document with the same name is still considered a prior version, so uploading a file whose name matches a trashed document will link a new v2 to a deleted v1 without user awareness.

Folder upload (folderInputRef) reads webkitRelativePath but only the flat file list is passed to runUploads — sub-directory structure inside the uploaded folder is ignored and all files land in the current folder.
No MIME-type validation occurs before upload; any file type can be placed in any folder, including placing executable files in the Specs or Plans folders.

leaves.name: system_kind enum on document_folders controls role-gated upload
acceptance: system_kind column is a CHECK-constrained text column accepting 10 values: plans, specs, rfis, submittals, shop_drawings, change_orders, daily_reports, photos, as_builts, correspondence. Inspectors may only upload to photos or daily_reports system folders; managers/admins can upload anywhere.

anchors.region: 123-137 (Inspectors upload to photos and daily_reports RLS policy)

leaves.evidence: DB enforces system_kind via CHECK constraint. TypeScript SystemKind union type mirrors the 10 allowed values. inspectorCanUploadHere checks selectedFolder.system_kind against 'photos'|'daily_reports'. RLS policy 'Inspectors upload to photos and daily_reports' enforces the same constraint server-side.
gaps: system_kind is stored as text not a Postgres enum; the CHECK constraint enforces valid values but the Supabase-generated TypeScript types in integrations/supabase/types.ts may use string rather than the narrower SystemKind union — silent widening if the generated types are not kept in sync with useDocuments.ts.

The inspector upload RLS policy grants INSERT to any authenticated project member when the target folder's system_kind is in ('photos','daily_reports'). It does not restrict UPDATE or DELETE for inspectors — an inspector who can insert can also soft-delete their own uploads only if deleted_by=auth.uid(), but the policy only covers INSERT; no explicit DENY exists for inspectors attempting DELETE on their own rows.

KIND_HINTS is a UI-only constant in Documents.tsx with no server-side backing; if a future system_kind is added to the DB constraint, it will silently display no hint tooltip in the folder tree sidebar.

leaves.name: block-nonempty-delete trigger prevents deleting non-empty folders
acceptance: DELETE on document_folders raises an exception if the folder contains any documents (any deleted_at status) or any subfolders. Trigger name: trg_document_folders_block_nonempty. Function: document_folders_block_nonempty_delete.
leaves.evidence: document_folders_block_nonempty_delete is a BEFORE DELETE trigger that checks documents.folder_id = OLD.id (no deleted_at filter — includes soft-deleted) and document_folders.parent_id = OLD.id. RAISE EXCEPTION on either condition. Trigger is DROP-then-CREATE idempotent.
gaps: The trigger checks documents WHERE folder_id = OLD.id with no deleted_at filter, meaning a folder containing only soft-deleted (trashed) documents cannot be deleted even after the user considers those documents 'gone'. The user must empty trash or hard-delete the trashed documents in the folder before the folder can be removed.

The exception message includes the folder name via OLD.name concatenation. If the folder name contains a percent sign or single quote it could cause unexpected string formatting — though RAISE EXCEPTION with %% quoting is handled by plpgsql, not raw SQL interpolation, so SQL injection is not a risk; the message may appear mangled in edge cases.

No client-side pre-flight check in deleteFolder (useFolders) warns the user before the DB round-trip fails; the error only surfaces after the mutation call returns the raw PostgreSQL exception as a destructive toast.

leaves.name: Soft-delete to Trash with Undo toast and Empty Trash
acceptance: Soft-deleting a document sets deleted_at; an Undo toast within the session restores it. 'Empty Trash' permanently removes DB rows and storage blobs. Trash view shows all deleted documents for the project.
leaves.evidence: softDeleteWithUndo bulk-updates deleted_at and deleted_by then shows a ToastAction 'Undo' that nulls both columns. runEmptyTrash DELETEs all project trash rows then calls storage.remove() on collected paths. useTrash queries documents where deleted_at IS NOT NULL.
gaps: softDeleteWithUndo in Documents.tsx bypasses the deleteDocument mutation in useDocuments.ts (which invalidates trash/folder-count query keys) and directly calls supabase.from('documents').update() — the Undo path similarly calls supabase directly. The hook mutation is therefore only partially used; two delete code paths exist with slightly different query invalidation patterns.

runEmptyTrash collects storage_path values from the in-memory trash array — if the trash query is stale when Empty Trash is triggered, recently trashed files whose trash query hasn't refreshed will have their DB rows deleted but their blobs orphaned.

The Undo toast has no timeout guard beyond the default toast duration (~5 s). If the user undoes after the toast has visually disappeared but before it is fully dismissed, the undo click handler still fires — correct behaviour — but if the page navigates away in that window the undo is silently lost.

leaves.name: Version history drawer and restore
acceptance: Version history drawer shows the full chain of replaces_document_id links in descending order. Clicking 'Restore' creates a new head version (source_kind='restore') pointing at the older blob.
leaves.evidence: fetchDocumentVersions selects all project documents (no folder filter) and walks the replaces_document_id chain from currentDocId backwards. restoreVersion inserts a new row with version=head.version+1, replaces_document_id=head.id, source_kind='restore'.
gaps: fetchDocumentVersions fetches ALL documents for a project (line 362: .eq('project_id', projectId) with no folder filter) and walks the chain in JS. For large projects this is O(N) rows transferred on every version drawer open.
Circular replaces_document_id chains (possible if DB rows are manipulated outside the app) would cause fetchDocumentVersions to loop infinitely — no cycle detection guard.

restoreVersion inserts a new row pointing to older.storage_path. It does not check whether that storage path still exists in the bucket — a restore of a version whose blob was deleted (e.g., empty-trash then DB rows still exist because only DB delete ran) will succeed at the DB level but produce a broken document entry.

leaves.name: Inline PDF and image preview modal via signed URL
acceptance: PDF and image documents open in a signed-URL preview modal without downloading. Non-previewable types trigger browser download. Signed URLs have 1-hour TTL.
leaves.evidence: isPreviewable returns true for image/* MIME or application/pdf or .pdf extension. getDownloadUrl calls createSignedUrl with 3600 s TTL. Preview modal renders an
gaps: PDF preview uses <iframe src=signedUrl>. Safari on iOS does not support inline PDF rendering in iframes — the PDF triggers a download instead of rendering, silently degrading to the same behaviour as a non-previewable file.

Signed URL TTL is 3600 s. If a user keeps the preview modal open for >1 hour the iframe src silently expires; no refresh mechanism exists. On a page reload the URL is regenerated, but mid-session expiry is not handled.

isPreviewable gates on mime_type starting with 'image/' but HEIC files (common on iOS) have mime_type 'image/heic'; browser cannot render HEIC natively on non-Safari browsers — the preview will display a broken image.

leaves.name: Multi-select bulk download and bulk soft-delete
acceptance: Multi-select checkboxes allow select-all and per-row selection. Bulk download opens each file in a new tab staggered by 250 ms. Bulk soft-delete moves all selected to Trash with a single Undo toast.
leaves.evidence: selectedIds Set tracks selection. toggleAll selects/deselects all filteredDocs. bulkDownload iterates selectedDocs and opens window.open() with 250 ms stagger. runBulkDelete delegates to softDeleteWithUndo(selectedDocs).
gaps: bulkDownload uses window.open() per file — browsers with popup blockers will suppress all but the first window.open() call even with the 250 ms stagger, silently failing to download most files in a bulk selection.

selectedIds is cleared when selectedFolderId changes (line 225 effect) but not when filteredDocs changes due to search — a user can search, select results, clear the search, and still have invisible (now off-screen) IDs in selectedIds that get bulk-deleted.
No size cap on bulk download; selecting and downloading thousands of files calls window.open N times with no cap or warning.

docDrift.claim: Stream doc §Surfaces lists documents table with 'deleted_at / deleted_by (soft delete)' as part of the initial CREATE TABLE.
docDrift.actual: deleted_at and deleted_by were added in a separate migration (20260524182507) as ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN. The initial CREATE TABLE in 20260524174837 does not include these columns.
docDrift.recommendation: Note in stream doc that soft-delete columns arrived in a follow-up migration.

docDrift.claim: Stream doc §Current state — 'Folder tree correctly renders nested hierarchy from parent_id; system folders sort before user folders alphabetically.'
docDrift.actual: Confirmed correct. buildTree sorts by is_system desc then name asc within each parent group. useFolders query orders by is_system desc, name asc.

docDrift.claim: Stream doc §Risks #2 — 'Blob orphan risk on insert failure — runUploads does a best-effort remove on insert failure, but the useDocuments.uploadFiles mutation does the same; the duplicate path means two slightly different cleanup paths could diverge.'
docDrift.actual: Confirmed accurate. Both runUploads (Documents.tsx:376-378) and uploadFiles (useDocuments.ts:192-194) independently catch insert errors and call storage.remove(). They are called in different contexts so they do not double-execute for the same upload, but divergence remains possible.
docDrift.recommendation: No correction required; risk is accurately stated.

docDrift.claim: Stream doc §Surfaces — 'public/project-documents — Storage bucket; paths follow {projectId}/{docId}.{ext}'
docDrift.actual: Confirmed: runUploads line 357 and uploadFiles line 171 both construct path as `${projectId}/${id}.${extOf(file.name)}` where id is a fresh UUID. Path convention matches.

docDrift.claim: Stream doc §Current state — 'Folder move — moveFolder mutation present in useFolders but drag-and-drop UI is absent; move is available only for documents via a modal.'
docDrift.actual: Confirmed: moveFolder mutation exists (useDocuments.ts:96-104) and is exported, but no drag-source, drop-target, or modal in Documents.tsx invokes moveFolder. Document move-to-folder modal (moveDocModal) calls moveDocument, not moveFolder.

docDrift.claim: Stream doc §Acceptance criteria — 'Folder file counts in the sidebar reflect only non-deleted, non-superseded (head) documents.'
docDrift.actual: Confirmed: folderCountsQuery (Documents.tsx:173-192) filters .is('deleted_at', null), computes replaced IDs set, and excludes non-head rows from counts.

docDrift.actual: Migration 20260524174837 §5 includes a DO $$ block that inserts document rows for existing projects' pdf_storage_path (into Plans folder, source_kind='legacy_plan_pdf') and specs_storage_path (into Specs folder, source_kind='legacy_specs_pdf').
